title: Nobody Is Saying Why OpenAI and Anthropic Had Outages Today
gist: Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI's Grok all suffered coinciding outages on the same Thursday morning, with xAI's SpaceX apologizing to 'impacted compute partners' -- a reference to its May compute partnership with Anthropic -- yet none of the three companies confirmed a shared root cause, and major infrastructure providers (Cloudflare, AWS, Azure) reported no incidents.

themes.theme: Simultaneous frontier-model outages and opaque root cause

insights.claim: Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI all experienced outages on the same Thursday morning (roughly 6:23am-10:05am PT across the three), with Google Gemini also facing scattered unconfirmed outage reports -- an unusual multi-vendor coincidence across nearly the entire frontier-AI-chatbot market in one morning.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Simultaneous outages across nearly all frontier AI providers signal potential systemic fragility (shared infrastructure dependency or correlated failure modes) in AI-chatbot infrastructure that enterprise customers relying on any single provider should weigh for redundancy planning.

insights.claim: SpaceX (xAI's parent) publicly apologized to its 'impacted compute partners' following the Memphis compute center outage -- a likely reference to Anthropic and xAI's compute partnership with SpaceX announced in May -- yet neither OpenAI nor Anthropic confirmed any external/shared cause for their own outages.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: The SpaceX apology to 'compute partners' hints at a possible shared infrastructure dependency between xAI and Anthropic via SpaceX, which -- if real -- would represent an underappreciated single point of failure risk across two major AI labs, though it remains unconfirmed by the companies themselves.
insights.quote: We’d also like to apologize to our impacted compute partners.

insights.claim: OpenAI attributed its outage to a 'routing error' beginning ~7:43am PT that made ChatGPT and Codex unavailable for some users, resolved by ~8:17am PT (about 34 minutes); Anthropic reported 'elevated errors' on Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5 starting 6:23am PT, marked resolved by 9:16am PT (about 3 hours), with Claude Sonnet 5 briefly affected after 9am PT; xAI's Grok outage ran from 6:30am to 10:05am PT (about 3.5 hours).
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Outage duration is a concrete reliability data point across providers -- OpenAI's fix was notably faster (34 min) than Anthropic's and xAI's (multi-hour), a relevant signal for enterprise SLA risk comparisons between AI vendors.

insights.claim: Major internet infrastructure providers that typically cause multi-customer outages -- Cloudflare, Amazon Web Services, and Microsoft Azure -- reported no incidents on the day of the coinciding AI outages, undercutting the typical explanation (shared CDN/cloud vendor failure) for simultaneous multi-company outages.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Ruling out the standard shared-infrastructure explanation leaves the coincidence unexplained, which is itself a signal worth monitoring: either an unreported shared dependency exists, or frontier AI providers are independently hitting reliability limits around the same load/scaling thresholds.
